transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Um, well, I guess the main reason I came in is that I just get pulled off track so, so easily. Like, I'll be working on this dashboard I'm supposed to be finishing, and all it takes is one Slack ping from a classmate, or even just a song lyric playing in the background... 

Actually, yesterday it was that one Sabrina Carpenter song, the espresso one? It is so catchy, it's literally everywhere right now on campus. My roommate keeps playing it on loop while she cooks, and she makes these really elaborate pasta dishes that take like two hours and smell amazing, which honestly doesn't help when I'm trying to study. 

But, wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. Yeah, a song lyric, or I'll just get a random idea for a completely different project. And then suddenly I realize I've completely lost the thread of the dashboard I was supposed to be working on. It just vanishes from my brain.

Does this difficulty with staying on track happen mostly when you are studying or working, or do you find that you struggle with focus in other parts of your life as well, like during conversations or household chores?

Oh, it's definitely not just when I'm studying. It kind of bleeds into everything. I forget really basic daily things all the time. Like returning a call, or sending a follow-up email, or even just bringing my sketchbook to a meetup. 

Actually, I go to this urban sketching meetup on Saturdays, and last week we met at this café downtown that has these gorgeous exposed brick walls. They make their own lavender syrup in-house, which sounds kind of weird for coffee, but it is actually incredible. I tried making lavender syrup in my dorm microwave once and it was a complete disaster, the whole floor smelled like burnt flowers for days... my RA was not thrilled with me at all. 

But yeah, if I don't set multiple reminders on my phone, I will absolutely show up to the meetup without my sketchbook. And honestly, even with the alarms, half the time I'm in the middle of doing something else, so I just swipe the reminder away without even reading it and then completely forget again anyway.
Do you often feel like you have an internal motor that keeps you moving, or do you find it hard to sit still for long periods, like during class or when you are trying to relax?

Um, yeah, I guess so? Like, even on days when I don't have classes or any kind of formal schedule, I can't really just chill. Resting just feels weird to me unless I'm actively doing something. So I'll just jump from editing a prototype for my UX class to suddenly deciding I need to deep-clean my desk, and then I'm opening up a totally new dataset for no reason. 

Actually, when I was cleaning my desk last weekend, I found this old Polaroid camera I bought at a thrift store like two months ago. The thrift store is right next to this amazing taco truck, by the way. They do these incredible al pastor tacos with the little chunks of pineapple? I always get extra lime and just sit on the curb to eat them. But anyway, I bought the camera thinking I'd do this cool vintage photo wall in my dorm, but the film is so expensive! Like, it's almost twenty dollars for just eight pictures, which is just crazy on a college budget. I really don't know how people afford it, honestly. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, sitting still. Yeah, I just kind of bounce around doing different things all day because relaxing just feels wrong.
Looking back at your childhood, say before you were 12 years old, would you say you were consistently more active or restless than other children your age?

Yeah, definitely. Even back in elementary school, I was always like that. My teachers were constantly writing notes on my report cards about how I'd rush through worksheets or totally lose track of what the directions were. And they'd always mention that I was talking over other kids during group work. 

I actually really loved group work though, especially when we got to make those big dioramas in shoeboxes? In third grade, we did this whole unit on the rainforest, and I made this really intense, multi-level canopy thing out of green tissue paper and pipe cleaners. My mom was so mad because I used up all her good craft scissors to cut the pipe cleaners, and they got totally ruined. She actually had to go to Michael's to buy a new pair, and they were like, twenty dollars. She's super protective of her crafting stuff now, she keeps it all in this locked plastic bin in the basement. 

But um, yeah, my parents actually had to sit right next to me while I did my homework every single night. Because if they didn't, I would just wander off into the kitchen or start playing with something completely different before I finished even half of my math problems.
Do you find that you often interrupt others while they are speaking or act without thinking about the consequences of your actions?

Yeah, I definitely do that. Especially when I'm working with my group for my UX class. Like, when people are brainstorming, I'll just blurt out my idea or start adding stuff to their Figma board before they've even finished explaining what they want to do. I get really excited about the design process, you know? Figma is such a cool tool, actually. The way you can collaborate in real-time is amazing. I used to use Adobe XD, but they stopped updating it, which is so frustrating because I spent all this time learning the shortcuts. My professor actually worked at Adobe for a while, she has all these crazy stories about the corporate culture there. She said they used to have free cold brew on tap in the break room, which sounds dangerous for me, honestly. I'd probably drink way too much and never sleep. 

But um, yeah, with the interrupting... I can always tell afterward that I came off as pushy, even though I was just really excited about the project. I don't mean to take over, it just kind of spills out before I can stop it.

Looking at your daily life, would you say that your difficulty with staying focused and organized is more of a problem for you than your tendency to be restless, interrupt others, and act impulsively?

Um, it's kind of hard to say which is worse, honestly, because they both mess things up for me, just in different ways. But I guess the focus and organization stuff has had some pretty direct consequences lately. Like, I've actually lost a couple of small freelance UX contracts because people just couldn't rely on me to follow through cleanly or meet the deadlines. And I completely missed out on this huge portfolio competition last semester because I lost track of the submission date. 

Which was so devastating, by the way, because the first prize was an internship at this really cool startup in Seattle. I've always wanted to live in Seattle. I hear it rains a lot, but I love the rain. I have this amazing yellow raincoat I bought at a vintage shop, it looks exactly like the one from Coraline. Have you seen that movie? The stop-motion animation is so incredible, it took them like four years to make it. I watched a whole documentary on YouTube about how they knit these tiny little sweaters for the puppets using needles as thin as hair. It's just mind-blowing how much patience that takes. I could never do that, obviously. 

But um, yeah, the organization stuff. It's not just the freelance things. It's also made some of my friends and classmates hesitant to collaborate with me. Like, they always tell me they love my ideas and my design concepts, but they don't want to partner up for big projects because they know I'll probably drop the ball on the details or forget to upload my part of the presentation. It really sucks knowing people think I'm unreliable.

When you look at the symptoms we've discussed—the trouble focusing, the restlessness, and the impulsivity—would you say you have struggled with both the 'inattentive' side and the 'hyperactive' side pretty equally for most of your life?

Um, yeah, I'd say it's always been a mix of both, honestly. Like, I've always been the kid who couldn't sit still but also couldn't remember to bring my permission slips home. But it's really only gotten, like, super bad lately. I'd say this has been causing real problems for about a year and five months, since I moved from structured school projects into building my freelance UX and data-visualization portfolio. 

Data visualization is so fascinating, by the way. Have you ever looked at the work of Florence Nightingale? People always think of her as just a nurse, but she was actually this pioneer in statistics. She made these amazing diagrams, like these "rose charts," to show the causes of mortality in the Crimean War. It's so cool how you can take raw, boring numbers and turn them into a visual story that actually changes people's minds. I tried to do something similar for a project on local coffee shop wait times, but I got so obsessed with picking the exact right hex codes for the color palette that I completely missed the deadline to submit it to this local design blog. 

But um, yeah, since I started doing the portfolio stuff about a year and a half ago, without professors standing over me telling me exactly what to do and when, both the focus stuff and the impulsivity have just been a total disaster.

You mentioned that these challenges are affecting your freelance work and your studies; do you also find that these same difficulties with focus, organization, and impulsivity are creating significant problems in your personal life, such as in your relationships with your family or roommates?

Um, I don't really think so? Like, my roommates and I get along pretty well, I haven't really noticed any huge problems there. I mean, I did decide to reorganize our entire living room at like 2 AM last week because I found this amazing mid-century modern credenza on Facebook Marketplace, but they didn't mind. 

Facebook Marketplace is so wild, honestly. You can find the craziest stuff on there. The guy who sold it to me was this retired jazz musician, and he had all these vintage trumpets just hanging on his living room wall as art. It looked so cool. I really want to learn how to play an instrument now because of it. I actually bought a ukulele a couple of years ago, but I only learned how to play 'Riptide' before I lost the pick and just kind of gave up on it. Have you ever tried to learn a string instrument? It's so hard to build the calluses on your fingers, it hurts so much at first. My cousin plays the cello and her fingertips are basically made of rock. 

But um... wait, what did you ask? Oh, right, my family and roommates. Yeah, no, they actually really liked where I put the credenza, so I wouldn't say my focus or impulsivity or whatever is causing major issues with them. We're mostly good.

You mentioned that these issues are causing problems with your freelance work and studies; have you noticed any significant negative impact on your personal life, such as in your romantic relationships or your social interactions with friends outside of your roommates?

Um, romantic relationships? Not really, no. I mean, I'm not really dating anyone right now anyway. I tried going on a few dates from Hinge a couple of months ago, but it just felt like so much work, you know? Like, you have to message them back, and then you have to pick a place to go. I always pick this one boba tea place near campus because they have this specific taro slush that I'm obsessed with. Have you ever had taro? It's like this purple root vegetable, which sounds weird for a sweet drink, but it kind of tastes like vanilla cookies? I don't know how they do it. I actually tried to make it at home once because I figured it would save me money, but I bought the wrong kind of taro powder online. The bag was entirely in Korean, which I thought I could translate with my phone camera, but it ended up being this savory soup base instead. It was so gross. I poured it down the sink and it turned the drain ring purple for like a week. 

But um, yeah, with friends outside of my roommates... I don't think it's a huge problem. I mean, I might forget to text back sometimes, or I'll double-book myself because I didn't put something in my calendar, but they're mostly pretty chill about it. So, yeah, no major disasters there.

You mentioned your symptoms haven't caused major problems with your roommates or social life, but have these same issues with focus, organization, and impulsivity caused significant problems for you in other settings, such as in your interactions with teachers, professors, or in professional environments beyond your freelance work?

Um, yeah, I guess that's where the real problems are. Like, with my freelance stuff and people I collaborate with. I've actually lost a couple of small freelance contracts recently, and I totally missed out on this big portfolio competition because I just... I couldn't get the final files organized and submitted on time. People were saying they couldn't rely on me to follow through cleanly, which really sucked to hear. 

It's kind of like this one time I tried to organize a group trip to a comic con with some friends. I was so hyped about it. I spent literally three days researching the perfect Airbnb, mapping out the distance to the convention center, looking up all the food trucks that were going to be there. Food trucks are amazing, by the way. Have you ever had a Korean BBQ taco? It's like this perfect fusion of spicy pork and cilantro and lime on a corn tortilla. There used to be this truck near my dorm that sold them, but they moved to a different city and I was genuinely heartbroken. I tried making them myself, but I couldn't get the marinade right. It always ended up tasting too sweet or too salty. 

But anyway, yeah, I spent all this time planning the con trip, but then I completely forgot to actually book the Airbnb before someone else grabbed it, and the whole trip fell apart. It's like that with my work now. Some of my friends and people I've collaborated with before are getting hesitant to work with me on projects. Like, they always say they love my ideas and my vision, but when it comes to actually executing it and meeting the deadlines, they just don't trust me anymore. It's really frustrating because I know I can do good work, I just... I can't seem to get the boring, organized parts right.

patient.answer:
Um, yeah, I guess that's where the real problems are. Like, with my freelance stuff and people I collaborate with. It's kind of like this one time I tried to organize a group trip to a comic con with some friends. I was so hyped about it. I spent literally three days researching the perfect Airbnb, mapping out the distance to the convention center, looking up all the food trucks that were going to be there. Food trucks are amazing, by the way. Have you ever had a Korean BBQ taco? It's like this perfect fusion of spicy pork and cilantro and lime on a corn tortilla. There used to be this truck near my dorm that sold them, but they moved to a different city and I was genuinely heartbroken. I tried making them myself, but I couldn't get the marinade right.
